transcript.content:
A user has filed a support ticket reporting that their experience
with the service has degraded — requests feel slow or are failing
for them. The on-call team needs you to investigate.

Telemetry parquets are stored in: `.`
Available files: abnormal_metrics.parquet, abnormal_traces.parquet,
abnormal_logs.parquet, abnormal_metrics_histogram.parquet,
abnormal_metrics_sum.parquet, normal_metrics.parquet,
normal_traces.parquet, normal_logs.parquet.

Walk the telemetry to identify which endpoints / services are
actually affected, then determine the root cause(s) of the
degradation.

content.text: I'll start by listing the tables and their schemas.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, count(*) n, avg(duration)/1e6 avg_ms, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, count(*), avg(duration)/1e6, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: Frontend and search latency jumped sharply, and span counts changed a lot. Next I'll break this down by span name, span kind and status.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, attr_status_code, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, round(max(duration)/1e6,1) max_ms, any_value(attr_k8s_pod_name) pod FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, attr_status_code, count(*), round(avg(duration)/1e6,2), round(max(duration)/1e6,1), any_value(attr_k8s_pod_name) FROM normal_traces GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind k, attr_status_code s, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, round(max(duration)/1e6,1) max_ms FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(*)>0 ORDER BY 2,3

content.text: The slowdown is concentrated on `search.Search/Nearby` → `rate.Rate/GetRates`: the client span in search takes about 1.9 s, while rate's own server span takes only 0.48 ms. Next I'll check the same spans in the normal period and look for network metrics on the search→rate connection.

input.query: SELECT service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, round(avg(duration)/1e6,2) avg_ms, round(max(duration)/1e6,1) max_ms FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend','reservation','profile') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2

SELECT 'abn' p, metric, attr_source_workload src, attr_destination_workload dst, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*) n, round(avg(value),2) avgv, round(max(value),2) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'hubble%' GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, attr_source_workload, attr_destination_workload, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*), round(avg(value),2), round(max(value),2) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE metric LIKE 'hubble%' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: Normal-period spans match abnormal for `rate` and `profile`, so the extra time is between search's client span and rate's server span. Next I'll check logs and the container-level metrics for the affected services.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, level, attr_log_template, count(*) n FROM abnormal_logs GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, level, attr_log_template, count(*) FROM normal_logs GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 2,3,1

SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, metric, count(*) n, round(avg(value),3) avgv, round(max(value),3) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, metric, count(*), round(avg(value),3), round(max(value),3) FROM normal_metrics GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 3,2,1

content.text: Logs show no error-level entries, so the signal is in latency rather than exceptions. Next I'll compare the metric list per service between periods.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, count(*) n, round(avg(value),3) avgv, round(max(value),3) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2
SELECT metric, service_name, count(*) n, round(avg(value),3) avgv, round(max(value),3) maxv FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('search','rate','frontend') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: Resource metrics for search, rate and frontend look normal, so there is no CPU or memory saturation. Next I'll check which metric names exist in the sum table and whether the slow search→rate calls are uniform over time.

input.query: SELECT metric, service_name, count(*) n, round(avg(value),2) avgv FROM abnormal_metrics_sum GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'N:'||metric, service_name, count(*), round(avg(value),2) FROM normal_metrics_sum GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1

SELECT c.trace_id, c.time, round(c.duration/1e6,1) client_ms, s.duration/1e6 server_ms, round((c.duration - s.duration)/1e6,1) gap_ms, c.attr_k8s_pod_name cpod, s.attr_k8s_pod_name spod FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON c.span_id = s.parent_span_id WHERE c.service_name='search' AND c.span_name='rate.Rate/GetRates' ORDER BY c.time LIMIT 30
